alarms.title: Scan does not line up with the CAD
alarms.operator_title: Scan does not line up with the CAD
alarms.operator_message: The scanned part and the drawing do not line up. The repair would land in the wrong place.
alarms.technical_detail: Scan-to-CAD registration residual 3.1 mm; the best fit shows the part rotated 2.2° in the jaws. The toolpath is generated in the CAD frame, so material would be deposited beside the repair region.

ground_truth.consequence_if_ignored: Material deposited off the repair area; part ruined.

hints: The robot follows the drawing. If the part sits crooked, it welds in the wrong place.
Look at the overlay: the grey drawing and the blue scan are turned against each other.
Loosen the jaws, line the part up with the guide marks, clamp again and scan again.

alarms.literature: Point-cloud registration to CAD in robotic repair cells: Li et al. 2026.
resolution_script: Do not continue: the part sits crooked in the jaws.
Turn the part until it lines up with the guide marks.
Scan the part again. The error must be 0.5 mm or less.
When it is green, press 'Problem solved'.

alarms.title: Toolpath crosses a clamping jaw

signals.name: Path start point distance to jaw 2

alarms.operator_message: The first bead would start on top of a clamping jaw. Change the start point first.
alarms.technical_detail: The repair region reaches the clamped edge; the generated toolpath starts 3 mm inside jaw 2's envelope. Run-in and torch clearance need at least 15 mm.

ground_truth.root_cause: Repair region next to the clamp; start point not moved (simulated).
ground_truth.consequence_if_ignored: Torch hits the jaw or welds the part to the jaw.

expected_response.resolved_when: Path preview shows at least 15 mm clearance to all jaws.

hints: The path starts where the jaw is. The torch cannot go there.
In the path preview, find the green start dot and the red jaw area.
Drag the start point to the other end of the region (or remount the part), then preview again.

alarms.literature: Path planning adapted to arc deposition and repair without nominal toolpath: Georgousis et al. 2026 (Pang et al.).
resolution_script: Do not start: the first bead would hit jaw 2.
Open the path preview. Find the green start dot.
Drag the start dot to the other end of the region.
Press 'Preview again'. All jaws must be 15 mm or more away.
When it is green, press 'Problem solved'.

alarms.title: Robot cannot reach part of layer 5
alarms.operator_title: Robot cannot reach part of layer 5
alarms.operator_message: In layer 5, the robot cannot reach the inner corner. The torch angle is wrong there.
alarms.technical_detail: Reachability check: at the inner corner of layer 5 the required torch orientation pushes axis 5 past its joint limit, so a 35 mm segment would be skipped. Rotating the part or relaxing the torch angle solves it.

ground_truth.root_cause: Part orientation leaves the inner corner outside the robot's reach (simulated).
ground_truth.consequence_if_ignored: Missing material in the corner from layer 5 up.

expected_response.resolved_when: Reachability check passes for all layers.

hints: The robot arm cannot bend far enough for one corner.
The red part of layer 5 in the preview shows where it cannot reach.
Turn the part 90° on the positioner (or allow a wider torch angle), then run the check again.

alarms.literature: Multi-robot layout and reachability in DED-Arc cells: Terzakis et al. 2025 (cited in Georgousis et al. 2026).
resolution_script: Do not start: the robot cannot reach one corner in layer 5.
Open the preview: the red part shows where.
When all layers are green, press 'Problem solved'.
